gloss: key money, gift money to landlord

definitions.explanation: A non-refundable payment made to the landlord as a 'thank you' or 'gift' when signing a rental contract in Japan, typically 1-2 months' rent.

examples.japanese: {礼金|れいきん}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{返金|へんきん}→返金：06130_henkin⟧⟦されません→する：00392_suru⟧。
{礼金|れいきん}⟦{一|いち}ヶ{月|げつ}→ヶ月：00956_kagetsu⟧、⟦{敷金|しききん}→敷金：06079_shikikin⟧⟦{一|いち}ヶ{月|げつ}→ヶ月：00956_kagetsu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{物件|ぶっけん}→物件：06743_bukken⟧。
examples.english: A property with one month's key money and one month's security deposit.

examples.japanese: {礼金|れいきん}⟦なし→なし：noentry⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{物件|ぶっけん}→物件：06743_bukken⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{増|ふ}えて→増える：01183_fueru⟧⟦いる→いる：00495_iru⟧。
examples.english: Properties with no key money are increasing.

notes:
COMPOUND: ⟦{礼|れい}→礼：02170_rei⟧ (thanks, gratitude) + ⟦{金|きん}→金：02666_kin⟧ (money)

CULTURAL NOTE: {礼金|れいきん} is a uniquely Japanese custom, especially common in the Kanto region (Tokyo area). It originated as a gift of gratitude to landlords but is often criticized as an unnecessary expense for renters.

COMMON PATTERNS:
・{礼金|れいきん}⟦ゼロ→ゼロ：01011_zero⟧ (zero key money)
・{礼金|れいきん}・⟦{敷金|しききん}→敷金：06079_shikikin⟧⟦なし→なし：noentry⟧ (no key money or deposit)

TRENDS: Many modern rental listings advertise '0⟦ゼロ→ゼロ：01011_zero⟧⟦{物件|ぶっけん}→物件：06743_bukken⟧' which have neither {礼金|れいきん} nor ⟦{敷金|しききん}→敷金：06079_shikikin⟧, making it easier to move in.
